name: code_search_repo
description: Search the repository for lines containing a literal, case-insensitive query. Use this before reading a specific file. Return at most 20 matching lines, capped by max_results. A valid query with no matches is a successful empty result: count is 0 and query_valid is true. A malformed query or invalid path glob produces an error rather than an empty success. The JSON result echoes query and includes count, query_valid, results, truncated, and index_age so the caller can tell whether matches were omitted or the search index may be stale.

query.description: Literal code text to search for, case-insensitively, not a regular expression. Maximum 200 characters; an empty or whitespace-only query is invalid. Use a specific identifier or error fragment to reduce irrelevant results and output tokens.

path_glob.description: Repository-relative file path glob, such as src/*.ts, or null to search all indexed files. Choose a glob when the file area is known; narrowing the scope reduces search work and output size. Invalid globs produce a repairable error.

max_results.description: Maximum number of matching lines to return, from 1 to 20. Use 10 for ordinary searches; higher values increase the response token cost.

deep.description: False searches the fast prebuilt index; true reads repository files from disk when freshness matters. Deep search costs more execution time and disk I/O.

response_format.description: Use concise for short excerpts and lower token cost. Use detailed when additional matching-line context is needed, at a higher token cost.

examples.note: Typical first search for a likely code identifier using the fast index and concise excerpts.
Search a known folder directly from disk if the index might be stale.
